summary: Jürgen Hanneder is an Indologist who studied under Alexis Sanderson (~1992–1996) and completed his PhD at the University of Marburg (~1992–1997). He held a post at the University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1999–2006) and became a professor at Marburg in ~2006.
Jürgen Neuß is an Indologist and historian-archaeologist who studied under Harry Falk and completed his PhD at the Free University of Berlin in 2007.

Jürgen Renn works in philosophy and history and archaeology. He studied at the Free University of Berlin (~1975–1982) and Technische Universität Berlin (~1983–1987), later holding posts at Humboldt University (1998), the Free University (2006), and MPIWG (~1994–2022).

K. A. Subramania Iyer was an Indologist, linguist, and philosopher who taught Dwijendra Nath Shukla. He served as a professor at the University of Lucknow (attested 1972, 1987) and as Vice-Chancellor of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University.
K. Balasubrahmanya Iyer was an Indologist who served as Managing Editor of the Journal of Oriental Research, Madras, and as Secretary of the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute (attested 1945).

Indologist and linguist K. Kunjunni Raja earned PhDs at Madras (under C. Kunhan Raja) and London (under John Brough). He served at the University of Madras (~1958–1980), Calgary Institute for the Humanities (~1980–1981), and Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute (attested 2001).

K. Meenakshi is an Indologist and linguist who earned a PhD under Madhukar Anant Mehendale at Savitribai Phule Pune University in 1964. She later held a post at Jawaharlal Nehru University (attested 1983).

K. Srinivasan is an Indologist who taught Hugo David, Steven Edward Lindquist, and Mattia Salvini. He held posts as professor at Ramakrishna Mission Vivekananda College (attested 2008) and at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute (attested 2020).

K. T. S. Sarao is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who earned PhDs from Delhi and Cambridge. He held posts at Kirori Mal College (1981), St Edmund's College, Cambridge (~1994–1995), and the University of Delhi (Prof., 1995).

K. V. Ramesh was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as Director of the Archaeological Survey of India (attested 1986–1987) and Honorary Director at the Oriental Research Institute, Mysore (attested 2012).
K. V. Rangaswami Aiyangar was an Indologist and historian-archaeologist. He served as Principal at Central Hindu College (~1935–1938) and at Banaras Hindu University (~1935–1939).

K. V. Sarma was an Indologist and historian-archaeologist who studied at the University of Kerala (~1937–1942). He held posts at ORI & Manuscripts Library (~1943–1951), University of Madras (1951–1962), and Sri Sarada Education Society Research Centre (~1988–2005).

K. Venkata Ramanan studied at Peking University under Yongtong Tang and Sentian Wang (1947–1949), under Prabodh Chandra Bagchi (1950), and at Harvard-Yenching. He held a D.Litt. and served as Professor of Philosophy at Visva-Bharati University.
Kaigen Noritake is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under Kenyu Mitomo. He served as an assistant professor (助教授) at Rissho University (attested 2007).

Kaikyoku Watanabe was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at the University of Strasbourg (~1900–1907). He later held posts at Toyo University (~1910–1926) and Taisho University (~1926–1933).

Kaiten Nukariya studied at Sendan-Rin, Keio, and Komazawa under Ryodo Nukariya. Active in Buddhist studies and philosophy, he lectured at Harvard (~1913–1915) and served at Komazawa University from 1919, becoming its first president (1925–1934).

Kaiun Shirodate is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He taught Koken Unno and Fujio Taniguchi, and held posts at Otani University as a full-time lecturer (attested 1986–1990) and professor (attested 1999–2002).
Kalidas Bhattacharyya was a scholar of philosophy and Indology who served as a professor (~1956–1971) and as Vice-Chancellor (attested 1966) at Visva-Bharati University.

Kalikinkar Datta was an Indologist and historian-archaeologist who taught Vishwanath Prasad Varma. He spent his career at Patna University (~1930–1965), where he later served as Vice-Chancellor (attested 1973).

Kalu Rinpoche, active in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, studied at Palpung Monastery (~1920–1931) under Lama Norbu Dondrup, Khakyab Dorje, and Tai Situ Pema Wangchok Gyalpo. He directed three-year retreats at Palpung (~1943–1955) and taught numerous prominent students.
